cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: File, object and block storage are the three ways a storage system exposes data. Block is a raw virtual disk attached to one server. File is a shared file system with folders and paths. Object stores data as objects with metadata and a key in a flat bucket over HTTP.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Block (EBS): low latency, high IOPS, for databases and boot volumes; protocols iSCSI, Fibre Channel, NVMe-oF. File (EFS): shared drives over NFS or SMB. Object (S3): almost unlimited scale and very durable, accessed by REST APIs, for media, backups and static assets.

questions.q: The S3 console shows folders. Is S3 a file system?
questions.a: No. Its namespace is flat; a key like users/42/photo.jpg is one string and folders are just prefixes. No real directories or file locking.
Block storage, for low latency and high IOPS.
